title: The most basic version of confounding
content: Pearl's Figure 4.1 separates the proposed causal path X -> Y from the spurious back-door fork X <- Z -> Y. Measured Z is an admissible adjustment set because it is not descended from X and blocks the only path entering X.

variables.name: Treatment or Cause (X)
variables.content: The proposed cause or treatment whose causal effect on Y is sought.

variables.name: Outcome (Y)
variables.content: The outcome affected by X and by the common cause Z.

variables.name: Confounder (Z)
variables.content: The lurking common cause that influences both treatment selection X and outcome Y.

arrows.because: The confounder influences who receives or exhibits X.
The same confounder independently influences Y.
This is the proposed causal effect whose estimate is mixed with the back-door association.
